articles.title: Introducing Cat Cvengros Second Harvest Food Bank
articles.summary: Cat Cvengros was honored with the Silicon Valley Business Journal's 40 Under 40 Award for her distinguished work and community involvement. As Vice President of Second Harvest of Silicon Valley, she significantly grew revenues and is recognized for her efforts against poverty. Additionally, she coordinates the San Jose Astronomical Association's (SJAA) School Star Party Program, expanding its reach to educate children about astronomy.

articles.title: M 35 Paper
articles.summary: This article recounts the journey of two high school students, Shashank and Shishir, whose project led to the discovery of an exoplanet and its publication in a prestigious journal. They utilized K2 mission data to find a planet orbiting a hot, A-type star in the M35 cluster region. Although initial findings suggested it was a cluster member, later data from the Gaia satellite showed it was not, yet the discovery of a planet around a hot star remains scientifically significant and a testament to citizen science.

articles.title: New Loaner Items
articles.summary: The SJAA Loaner Program has added two new donated Orion refractors to its collection: an ED80T Triplet and an ED66 Doublet. These lightweight and compact telescopes, suitable for both astronomical viewing/imaging and terrestrial observations, are now available for all SJAA members to try out.

articles.title: Critical Deployment of NASA Webb's Secondary Mirror a Success
articles.summary: NASA's James Webb Space Telescope successfully completed the critical deployment test of its secondary mirror support structure, marking a significant milestone before the observatory's final assembly. This test also confirmed the electronic connection for command delivery, ensuring the secondary mirror, vital for collecting and focusing light from the primary mirrors, is ready for its future deployment in space. This achievement brings Webb closer to its mission of revolutionary space science.

articles.title: The Two-by-Three Chair
articles.summary: This article details the design, construction, and field testing of a custom-built astronomy observing chair named "The Two-by-Three Chair." The chair prioritizes being cheap, lightweight, sturdy, comfortable, collapsible, and adjustable, utilizing kiln-dried 2x3 whitewood studs and other recycled materials. While largely successful in meeting its design goals, the author notes challenges with frequent assembly/disassembly due to softwood inserts and issues with paint sticking, leading to plans for future improved versions.

articles.title: SJAA Member Astrophoto Gallery
articles.summary: This article presents the SJAA (San Jose Astronomical Association) Member Astrophoto Gallery, showcasing various astrophotography images captured by members. Each entry details the celestial object photographed, the photographer's name, capture date, location, and the specific imaging telescope, camera, mount, and software used. Featured images include the Dark Shark nebula, Milky Way, Cygnus Wall, and VVB 34.

articles.title: Kid Spot
articles.summary: This article features astronomy-themed jokes for children and announces the beginning of scheduling for the SJAA's School Star Parties, urging both volunteers and schools to sign up. It also provides a detailed report on the recent Yosemite Star Party, describing successful dark sky observations of various celestial objects despite challenges with campground changes and a new issue with light pollution.

articles.title: From the Board of Directors
articles.summary: The SJAA Board of Directors provided updates on club activities, highlighting that the QuickSTARt program is on hold and the library is operational, while actively seeking more volunteers. Board meetings covered successful outreach events like the USS Hornet's Apollo 11 anniversary celebration, improvements to ITSP viewing conditions, the development of an official outreach policy, and planning for the 2020 events calendar, including an upcoming internship program for astronomy students.

articles.title: SJAA Library
articles.summary: The San Jose Astronomical Association (SJAA) offers diverse programs and resources for its members and the community, including a library of astronomy materials and various hands-on sessions. Offerings range from telescope repair services and regular solar and night sky observing events to beginner guidance programs and an equipment loaner program. Additionally, SJAA hosts special interest groups and workshops for astrophotography, alongside outreach initiatives like school star parties, catering to all age groups and experience levels.
